items.text: Extending a notion to topoi
Several candidate extensions of a notion (flatness, connectedness of a ring): discard one that is not stable under inverse image by morphisms of topoi.
Hakim (relative schemes of finite presentation over a ringed topos): two notions of flatness, not shown equal.
Relative schemes: not an algebraic structure in the sense used (underlying topological space, gluing).
Algebraic = a constructible species of structure.
Topological spaces: a limiting case, when non-small families of data are allowed.
A pseudo-functor on a 2-category $\Delta$: $\Delta$ must be fixed as a mathematical object; the representing object may leave it.
Hypertopoi
Sets have properties topoi lack, involving infinite inverse limits:
\textstyle\prod_i(\text{epimorphisms})\ \text{is an epimorphism}\quad(\text{like total disconnectedness})
\prod_{j}\coprod_{i\in I_j}X_{ij}=\coprod_{\varphi\in\prod_j I_j}\prod_{j}X_{j\varphi(j)}\ \ (\text{infinite products distribute over sums})
Second property: the projection of the topos to a point is essential, i.e. the constant-sheaf functor commutes with arbitrary products (like local connectedness).
Guess: such topoi are exactly the $\widehat C$ (limits are taken elementwise).
2-category $\Delta_{\mathrm{hyp}}$ of hypertopoi: morphisms = essential morphisms, commuting also with infinite inverse limits.
Aim: algebraic structures even with infinite inverse limits; the classifying hypertopos.
C\ \text{small with finite inverse limits},\qquad T(E)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{lex}}(C,E)
T(E)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta_{\mathrm{hyp}}}(?,E)\quad E\ \text{a hypertopos}
E=\widehat D,\quad D=\text{essential points of }E\ \text{(Karoubian, determined by }E)
\text{functor }R\to\widehat D\ \leftrightarrow\ R\times D\to\mathbf{Sets},\qquad R=\widehat C
For fixed element of $D$: a functor $R\to\mathbf{Sets}$ commuting with direct limits and finite inverse limits (= a point of $R$).
T(E)=\operatorname{Hom}(R,E)=\operatorname{Hom}\bigl(D,\ \mathrm{Pts}(R)\bigr)
\mathrm{Pts}(\widehat C)=\operatorname{Pro}C\qquad(\text{fibre functors: }\operatorname{Ind}(C^{\circ}))
\text{only candidate:}\quad(\operatorname{Pro}C)^{\wedge}\ \ (\text{essential points of }\widehat C)
$\operatorname{Pro}C$ is not small: leaves the universe; no small generators — a pseudo-hypertopos.
Groups: take the opposite category, then the hat — all functors from groups to sets; a pseudo-hypertopos that does the job.
Universes and galaxies
Universes need a very strong axiom of set theory (strictly inaccessible cardinals); logicians had seen no hope of a relative consistency proof.
\kappa>\aleph_0\ \text{strictly inaccessible: }\ \lambda<\kappa\Rightarrow2^\lambda<\kappa;\quad \lambda_i<\kappa,\ |I|<\kappa\Rightarrow\textstyle\sum\lambda_i<\kappa
Galaxies (Samuel’s idea): sets smaller than universes, with the union axiom weakened — as described, the idea is unclear.
Galaxies: easily shown to exist; weaker inaccessibility. Is category theory (injectives, homological algebra) possible with galaxies?
In practice only a few exponentials are needed: $2^{2^{2^c}}$, or $\aleph_0$ iterations.
Want a context with no new axioms of set theory and room for $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}(C,C')$, large categories.
Remark from the room: a well-defined abelian group (an Ext group) is a direct sum of cyclic groups under the continuum hypothesis — undecidable question.
